name: Data from Network Shared Drive
description: Adversaries may search network shares on computers they have compromised to find files of interest. Sensitive data can be collected from remote systems via shared network drives (host shared directory, network file server, etc.) that are accessible from the current system prior to Exfiltration. Interactive command shells may be in use, and common functionality within [cmd](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0106) may be used to gather information.

telemetry.name: Drive Access
telemetry.description: Access to a disk/drive device, including supported raw-read observations.
telemetry.collection_focus: For Windows raw reads, review Sysmon RawAccessRead (9); collect device path and process. Normal file I/O is a different source.

providers.name: Microsoft Sysmon
providers.scope: Windows event-based collection; enable the event types needed below.

providers.name: Linux Audit
providers.scope: Linux alternative for supported system-call and file events; different semantics and fields.

providers.name: Apple Endpoint Security clients
providers.scope: macOS alternative where the subscribed event exists; requires an entitled, approved client, not an iOS collector.

configuration: On a disposable Windows host, review the installed Sysmon schema and current configuration; merge scoped event filters into the existing policy rather than replacing it.
Forward Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational to the lab collector. Preserve event ID, timestamp, computer, process identifiers and the original event.
For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Event filtering and sensor versions change coverage. High-volume image-load and process-access collection needs tuning; endpoint events alone do not establish intent.

telemetry.anomaly_design: Per host role and user: rare process/object combinations, bursts of object access or modification, and ordered parent/action sequences. Compare maintenance windows and signed software rollout activity.

telemetry.name: File Access
telemetry.description: Access to file objects with user, process and access-right context.
telemetry.collection_focus: Enable Audit File System plus a narrow SACL on a lab directory; on Linux select path/syscall rules and join associated Audit records.

providers.name: Windows Security auditing
providers.scope: Policy-dependent account, object, task and logon records on the host that performs the operation.

configuration: Use a lab-only GPO under Computer Configuration → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Advanced Audit Policy Configuration. Enable the specific subcategory named below.
For object-level auditing, configure a narrow system access control list (SACL) on the test object in addition to policy. Do not audit an entire production directory by default.

Forward Security events from the responsible host or controller; retain subject and target identities, object identifiers, result and original XML. Confirm effective policy with auditpol /get /category:*.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: A policy checkbox alone does not guarantee an event. Host role, SACL, success/failure selection and audit policy precedence matter. Directory changes may arrive as multiple records.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per principal, host and object: unusual access/request rates, new principal-object relationships, and changes outside approved administration windows. Control for service accounts and scheduled directory maintenance.

telemetry.name: File Creation
telemetry.description: Creation or overwrite of a file at an observed path.
telemetry.collection_focus: Scope Sysmon FileCreate (11) to the lab directory; retain the process and file path. Differentiate creation/overwrite if the sensor can.

atlas_basic.title: T1039 Data from Network Shared Drive

strategies.name: Detection Strategy for Data from Network Shared Drive

analytics.name: Analytic 1145
analytics.guidance: Monitoring of file access to network shares (e.g., C$, Admin$) followed by unusual read or copy operations by processes not typically associated with such activity (e.g., PowerShell, certutil).

tuning.description: Organizations may use custom share paths outside of default C$, Admin$, etc.
Common toolsets vary; defenders should tailor to unusual processes for their environment.
Time of day and access duration may need to be tuned to reduce false positives.

analytics.name: Analytic 1146
analytics.guidance: Unusual access or copying of files from mounted network drives (e.g., NFS, CIFS/SMB) by user shells or scripts followed by large data transfer.

tuning.description: Organization-specific share mount paths may vary (/mnt/share1, /srv/data etc.)
May need to scope to service accounts or user ID patterns specific to enterprise policy.

analytics.name: Analytic 1147
analytics.guidance: Detection of file access from mounted SMB shares followed by copy or exfil commands from Terminal or script interpreter processes.

tuning.description: Script interpreters may vary (e.g., zsh, bash, python, osascript).
Network drive mount points may differ across enterprises.

software.name: CosmicDuke
software.description: [CosmicDuke](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0050) steals user files from network shared drives with file extensions and keywords that match a predefined list.(Citation: F-Secure Cosmicduke)

references.description: F-Secure Labs. (2014, July). COSMICDUKE Cosmu with a twist of MiniDuke. Retrieved July 3, 2014.

software.name: BADNEWS
software.description: When it first starts, [BADNEWS](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0128) crawls the victim's mapped drives and collects documents with the following extensions: .doc, .docx, .pdf, .ppt, .pptx, and .txt.(Citation: Forcepoint Monsoon)

references.description: Settle, A., et al. (2016, August 8). MONSOON - Analysis Of An APT Campaign. Retrieved September 22, 2016.

software.name: Ramsay
software.description: [Ramsay](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0458) can collect data from network drives and stage it for exfiltration.(Citation: Eset Ramsay May 2020)

references.description: Sanmillan, I.. (2020, May 13). Ramsay: A cyber‑espionage toolkit tailored for air‑gapped networks. Retrieved May 27, 2020.

software.name: Egregor
software.description: [Egregor](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0554) can collect any files found in the enumerated drivers before sending it to its C2 channel.(Citation: NHS Digital Egregor Nov 2020)

references.description: NHS Digital. (2020, November 26). Egregor Ransomware The RaaS successor to Maze. Retrieved December 29, 2020.

actors.name: APT28
actors.description: [APT28](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0007) has collected files from network shared drives.(Citation: Cybersecurity Advisory GRU Brute Force Campaign July 2021)

references.source_name: Cybersecurity Advisory GRU Brute Force Campaign July 2021
references.description: NSA, CISA, FBI, NCSC. (2021, July). Russian GRU Conducting Global Brute Force Campaign to Compromise Enterprise and Cloud Environments. Retrieved July 26, 2021.

actors.name: menuPass
actors.description: [menuPass](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0045) has collected data from remote systems by mounting network shares with net use and using Robocopy to transfer data.(Citation: PWC Cloud Hopper April 2017)

references.description: PwC and BAE Systems. (2017, April). Operation Cloud Hopper. Retrieved April 5, 2017.

actors.name: Gamaredon Group
actors.description: [Gamaredon Group](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0047) malware has collected Microsoft Office documents from mapped network drives.(Citation: ESET Gamaredon June 2020)(Citation: ESET Gamaredon Sept2024)

references.description: Boutin, J. (2020, June 11). Gamaredon group grows its game. Retrieved June 16, 2020.
Rusnák, Z. (2024, September 26). Cyberespionage the Gamaredon way: Analysis of toolset used to spy on Ukraine in 2022 and 2023. Retrieved October 30, 2024.

actors.name: Sowbug
actors.description: [Sowbug](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0054) extracted Word documents from a file server on a victim network.(Citation: Symantec Sowbug Nov 2017)

references.description: Symantec Security Response. (2017, November 7). Sowbug: Cyber espionage group targets South American and Southeast Asian governments. Retrieved November 16, 2017.

actors.name: BRONZE BUTLER
actors.description: [BRONZE BUTLER](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0060) has exfiltrated files stolen from file shares.(Citation: Secureworks BRONZE BUTLER Oct 2017)

references.description: Counter Threat Unit Research Team. (2017, October 12). BRONZE BUTLER Targets Japanese Enterprises. Retrieved January 4, 2018.

actors.name: Chimera
actors.description: [Chimera](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0114) has collected data of interest from network shares.(Citation: NCC Group Chimera January 2021)

references.description: Jansen, W . (2021, January 12). Abusing cloud services to fly under the radar. Retrieved September 12, 2024.

actors.name: Fox Kitten
actors.description: [Fox Kitten](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0117) has searched network shares to access sensitive documents.(Citation: CISA AA20-259A Iran-Based Actor September 2020)

references.description: CISA. (2020, September 15). Iran-Based Threat Actor Exploits VPN Vulnerabilities. Retrieved December 21, 2020.

actors.name: RedCurl
